# [TASK] Tests and accessibility pass: query highlighting

## Task
Test and accessibility pass for query highlighting.

## Scope
Coverage gaps left after #207-#209's own inline tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Component tests cover all three highlight categories rendering simultaneously in one query (`QueryHighlightOverlay.test.jsx`'s "renders three categories in one query with three distinct underline styles" test)
- [x] Dictated-query highlighting (transcript populates the field) is covered, not just typed input (`Search.test.jsx`, describe block "Search - dictated query hand-off (#199 AC5 / #210)": field population, immediate parse, overlay rendering, one-shot consumption, debounce cancellation, and stale-response discard for back-to-back dictated queries)
- [x] Automated accessibility check confirms the highlighted markup introduces no other WCAG violation (`QueryHighlightOverlay.test.jsx`'s axe test, all three categories rendered together) — axe-core has no rule that judges "color alone" (WCAG 1.4.1); that property is proven separately by #209 AC1's underline-style/weight assertions
- [x] Highlighting is legible in both light and dark mode (manual: Chromium screenshot of the search field with all three categories in one query — "a and not Batman" — in both themes via the dev server; dark mode uses `highlightStyles.js`'s three colors as designed, light mode's pre-existing `filter: invert(1)` inverts them to a different but still mutually distinct hue triplet; both themes stay distinguishable by underline shape and weight, not color alone)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 4

## Notes
`VoiceControl.jsx`'s "search" voice command used to run the search directly, bypassing `Search.jsx`'s field state and the whole highlighting pipeline, so AC2 needed a real fix, not just a test. Added a one-shot Redux hand-off (`dictatedQuery`/`dictatedQuerySubmitted`/`dictatedQueryConsumed` in `currentGenreOrCategory.js`) so a dictated query now runs through the same `runParse`/`runSearch` pipeline as a typed-and-Entered query. This also satisfies parent Story #199's AC5.

Actual effort was about 2x the 4-hour estimate: AC2 required fixing that wiring gap, not just adding tests against existing behavior.
